title: Biceps brachii
summary: A two-headed muscle on the front of the upper arm. It contributes to elbow bending and turning the forearm palm-up.

title: Brachialis
summary: An elbow flexor located across the front of the lower upper arm and elbow. Its distal attachment is on the ulna.

title: Triceps brachii
summary: The three-headed muscle along the back of the upper arm contributes to straightening the elbow.

title: Levator scapulae
summary: A muscle at the back and side of the neck that helps raise the medial angle of the scapula.

title: Deltoid
summary: A triangular muscle covering the front, back and lateral shoulder. Its portions contribute to raising the arm and moving it forward or backward.

title: Anterior deltoid
summary: The anterior portion of the deltoid contributes to drawing the arm forward with pectoralis major.

title: Posterior deltoid
summary: The posterior portion of the deltoid contributes to drawing the arm backward with teres major and latissimus dorsi.

title: Supraspinatus
summary: A muscle above the scapular spine that assists in raising the arm from the side and holding the humeral head in the glenoid cavity.

title: Infraspinatus
summary: A muscle below the scapular spine that rotates the humerus outward and assists in carrying the arm backward.

title: Teres minor
summary: A narrow muscle along the lateral scapular border that helps rotate the humerus outward and move the arm backward.

title: Subscapularis
summary: A triangular muscle on the front surface of the scapula that rotates the humerus inward.

title: Pectoralis major
summary: A fan-shaped muscle on the front of the upper chest that draws the arm toward the body and across the chest and rotates it inward.

title: Pectoralis minor
summary: A thin muscle beneath pectoralis major that draws the scapula downward and toward the chest.

title: Serratus anterior
summary: A muscular sheet between the ribs and scapula that carries the scapula forward and contributes to its rotation during arm raising.

title: Latissimus dorsi
summary: A broad muscle over the lower back that connects to the humerus and helps draw the arm backward, downward and inward in rotation.

title: Trapezius
summary: A broad muscle over the upper back and neck. Its portions help retract, elevate, depress and rotate the scapula.

title: Upper trapezius
summary: The upper trapezius fibers help elevate the point of the shoulder when the head is fixed.

title: Middle trapezius
summary: The middle trapezius fibers participate in scapular retraction and, with lower fibers, scapular rotation.

title: Lower trapezius
summary: The lower trapezius fibers assist scapular depression and participate with middle fibers in scapular rotation and retraction.

title: Rhomboid group
summary: Rhomboid major and minor connect the vertebral column to the medial scapula and act with trapezius fibers to retract the scapula.

title: Teres major
summary: A muscle from the inferior scapula to the humerus that assists latissimus dorsi in lowering the raised arm, drawing it backward and rotating it inward.

title: Gluteus maximus
summary: A broad superficial gluteal muscle described as extending the thigh and supporting the pelvis and trunk.

title: Gluteus medius
summary: A lateral pelvic muscle contributing to thigh abduction and pelvic support when standing on one limb.

title: Gluteus minimus
summary: A small gluteal muscle beneath gluteus medius, contributing to thigh abduction and one-limb pelvic support.

title: Tensor fasciae latae
summary: A muscle connected with the iliotibial band, described as tensing fascia and assisting thigh abduction and inward rotation.

title: Rectus femoris
summary: A quadriceps component contributing to knee extension and assisting hip flexion.

title: Vastus lateralis
summary: A quadriceps component contributing to knee extension.

title: Vastus medialis
summary: A quadriceps component contributing to knee extension.

title: Vastus intermedius
summary: A quadriceps component contributing to knee extension.

title: Biceps femoris
summary: A two-headed posterior thigh muscle contributing to knee flexion and outward rotation of the bent leg.

title: Biceps femoris — long head
summary: A named head of biceps femoris sharing its distal tendon; head-specific activation or isolation is not established here.

title: Biceps femoris — short head
summary: A named head of biceps femoris sharing its distal tendon; head-specific activation or isolation is not established here.

title: Semitendinosus
summary: A medial posterior thigh muscle with a long tendon, contributing to knee flexion and inward rotation of the bent leg.

title: Semimembranosus
summary: A medial posterior thigh muscle contributing to knee flexion and a smaller role in inward rotation of the bent leg.

title: Gastrocnemius
summary: A superficial two-headed calf muscle contributing to heel raising at the ankle and knee flexion.

title: Gastrocnemius — medial head
summary: A named head of gastrocnemius contributing to its shared calf muscle and calcaneal tendon.

title: Gastrocnemius — lateral head
summary: A named head of gastrocnemius contributing to its shared calf muscle and calcaneal tendon.

title: Soleus
summary: A broad calf muscle beneath gastrocnemius, contributing to heel raising and supporting the leg over the foot in standing.

title: Adductor magnus
summary: A large medial thigh muscle described in the historical source as contributing to thigh adduction.

title: Adductor longus
summary: A superficial triangular medial thigh muscle described as contributing to thigh adduction and flexion.

title: Adductor brevis
summary: A shorter medial thigh muscle described as contributing to thigh adduction and assisting thigh flexion.

title: Gracilis
summary: A thin superficial medial thigh muscle described as adducting the thigh and assisting knee flexion and inward leg rotation.

title: Pectineus
summary: A flat upper medial thigh muscle described as contributing to thigh adduction and assisting thigh flexion.

title: Tibialis anterior
summary: A front-of-leg muscle described as flexing the foot upward at the ankle and helping turn the medial border upward.

title: Deep hip external rotator group
summary: A labelled anatomical group comprising piriformis, obturator internus and externus, the two gemelli and quadratus femoris.

title: Sternocleidomastoid
summary: A paired muscle crossing the side of the neck, with sternal and clavicular heads.

title: Middle/lateral deltoid
summary: The central acromial portion of the deltoid, distinguished by its attachment and fiber arrangement.

title: Pectoralis major — clavicular portion
summary: The clavicular portion of pectoralis major; the historical description distinguishes its origin and tendon contribution.

title: Pectoralis major — sternocostal portion
summary: The sternal and costal portion of pectoralis major, with fibers converging into its shared humeral tendon.

title: Erector spinae group
summary: The historical Sacrospinalis group divides into iliocostalis, longissimus and spinalis columns along the back.

title: Multifidus
summary: A series of short fleshy and tendinous fascicles alongside the spinous processes, extending from sacrum to axis.

title: Coracobrachialis
summary: A small upper medial arm muscle sharing a coracoid origin with the short head of biceps.

title: Brachioradialis
summary: A superficial muscle on the radial side of the forearm, historically also called Supinator longus.

title: Wrist and finger flexor group
summary: A functional grouping of wrist and finger flexors. The source describes distinct actions for named flexors, rather than one action for every member.

title: Wrist and finger extensor group
summary: A functional grouping of wrist and finger extensors, with different named muscles acting at different joints.

title: Rectus abdominis
summary: A long flat paired muscle along the anterior abdomen, separated at the midline by the linea alba.

title: External oblique
summary: The superficial flat muscle of the lateral and anterior abdominal wall, with an aponeurosis joining at the linea alba.

title: Internal oblique
summary: A flat abdominal muscle beneath external oblique, with fibers and aponeurotic attachments that vary across its parts.

title: Transversus abdominis
summary: The innermost flat abdominal muscle in the historical description, lying immediately beneath internal oblique.

title: Quadratus lumborum
summary: A posterior abdominal-wall muscle with iliac, lumbar and last-rib attachments that vary between individuals.

title: Diaphragm
summary: A dome-shaped musculotendinous partition between the thoracic and abdominal cavities, converging into a central tendon.

title: Iliopsoas group
summary: Psoas major and iliacus converge through the psoas tendon near the hip. This grouping does not include the differently acting psoas minor.

title: Sartorius
summary: A narrow ribbon-like muscle crossing obliquely from the lateral upper thigh toward the medial knee.

title: Tibialis posterior
summary: A deep posterior-leg muscle whose tendon passes behind the medial ankle and spreads to several foot attachments.

title: Fibularis/peroneal group
summary: The peroneal/fibular muscles include longus and brevis in the lateral leg and tertius described with the anterior-leg muscles; their ankle actions differ.

summary: A named head of biceps brachii, distinguished by its proximal attachment and converging into the shared distal tendon.

summary: A named head of biceps brachii, distinguished by its proximal attachment and converging into the shared distal tendon.

summary: A named head of triceps brachii, distinguished by its origin and joining the shared insertion.

title: Consistency and adherence
summary: ACSM emphasizes regular resistance-training participation for healthy adults, with goals, enjoyment and safety guiding an achievable routine.

title: Muscle hypertrophy
summary: The ACSM summary distinguishes muscle-size goals from strength and power, and describes weekly training volume as a goal-dependent variable.

title: Training to muscular failure
summary: ACSM reports that reaching fatigue or momentary failure did not consistently change outcomes for the average healthy adult in its reviewed evidence.

title: Rest intervals
summary: In nine studies of healthy adults, pooled estimates suggested a small muscle-growth advantage for longer rather than very short rests, with substantial overlap and variation. The analysis did not establish a universal best rest duration.

title: Training splits
summary: The meta-analysis of fourteen studies in healthy adults found similar strength and muscle-growth changes with split and full-body schedules when training volume was matched. This does not establish equal results for every individual or unmatched workload.

title: Strength adaptation
summary: The ACSM review found improved strength versus no exercise; heavier loads and complete movement ranges enhanced this outcome.

title: Power development
summary: In the ACSM synthesis, moderate loads and a fast concentric phase favored power outcomes; the precise training context remains important.

title: Physical function
summary: The ACSM review reported improved gait speed, balance and several physical-function outcomes versus no exercise; power training also supported function.

title: Training volume
summary: Higher weekly set volume favored muscle growth in the ACSM synthesis; this does not establish each person’s ideal weekly amount.

title: Load and relative intensity
summary: Heavier relative loads favored voluntary strength in the ACSM review; load percentage does not describe how close a particular set finishes to failure.

title: Training frequency
summary: Multiple weekly sessions supported strength in the ACSM synthesis; frequency and total weekly set volume are different prescription variables.

title: Range of motion
summary: Complete movement ranges favored voluntary strength in the ACSM synthesis; the abstract does not establish one suitable range for every joint or circumstance.

title: Exercise order
summary: Earlier session placement favored voluntary-strength outcomes in the ACSM review; the result does not specify one exercise sequence for every goal.

title: Repetitions in reserve
summary: A scoping review found RIR scales contextually useful; estimates tended to be more accurate near task failure, with important population and exercise limitations.

title: Tempo and repetition duration
summary: The 2025 review found a small overall hypertrophy difference between faster and slower tempos, with uncertainty varying by study condition.

title: Superset
summary: Supersets shortened sessions and increased perceived exertion in the review; pooled chronic outcomes did not establish a clear advantage over traditional sets.

title: Drop set
summary: The 2026 synthesis found higher acute perceived exertion and lactate with drop sets, without a clear chronic strength, hypertrophy or endurance advantage.

title: Deloading
summary: Coaches proposed deload design principles by consensus; a separate trial of complete one-week cessation found less strength improvement than continuous training.

title: Specificity
summary: The authors describe adaptations as specific to the training stimulus, while noting carryover across muscular performance domains in nonadvanced trainees.

title: Progressive overload
summary: The discussion distinguishes initial benefit from continued longer-term progress: increasing a stimulus can support continued adaptation, but progression is not a prerequisite for every initial benefit.

title: Individual response
summary: The authors state that pooled group-level findings require individualization to goals, needs, experience and circumstances; the review does not predict each individual response.

title: Periodization
summary: The discussion reports uncertain overall strength conclusions, with one volume-equated review slightly favouring periodization. It does not establish a universal periodized-program advantage under appropriate overload.

title: Proximity to failure
summary: The authors propose near-failure or a target of two to three repetitions in reserve as a way to achieve sufficient effort; completing every set to muscular failure is not required for benefit.

title: Muscular endurance
summary: The overview reports improved muscular endurance with resistance training compared with no exercise; its reviewed analyses included standard and home-based training.
